Date January 4, 1937
FILE No. REG.
D. 7634

Subject "Deutsche Wochenschau," new German/English publication and its
editor Martin BAUMGARTEN.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by [Signature] D.S.P.

Forwarded herewith is the second and last issue of
"Deutsche Wochenschau." Its editor, Martin BAUMGARTEN,
apparently realised that with this issue the publication
was doomed to financial failure, consequent upon which his
partner, Dr. von MIORINI, withdrew his support.
Baumgarten left Shanghai on December 11, 1936 for Hankow
and Canton in an effort to seek more congenial employment.
Should he return to Shanghai his activities will be made the
subject of a further report.

现随函附上“Deutsche Wochenschau”的第二期暨最后一期。
其编辑 Martin BAUMGARTEN 显然意识到，随着这一期的出版，
该刊物注定要在财务上失败，因此他的合伙人 Dr. von MIORINI
撤回了支持。
Baumgarten 于1936年12月11日离开上海前往汉口
和广州，试图寻找更合适的工作。
若他返回上海，其活动将成为进一步报告的主题。

Date November 25, 1936.

Subject "Deutsche Wochenschau," new German/English publication and
its editor Martin BAUMGARTEN.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

（左侧手写批注：X Olive are time
by Xlt '36）

I forward herewith a specimen sample copy of "Deutsche
Wochenschau," a new German/English four-page newspaper that is
scheduled to make its initial appearance locally in the early
part of December, 1936. It will be non-political in tone and
will devote its columns to topical news and illustrations.
It is not being supported or subsidised by any local official
German organs, which maintain that the Ostasiatischer Lloyd
as a newspaper, is sufficient for the needs of the German
community here.
The editor and publisher of "Deutsche Wochenschau" is a
German, Martin BAUMGARTEN, born at Freiburg, Breisgau, 36 years
ago. He is not a Jew. Associated with him as a sleeping
partner in this journalistic venture is Dr. von MIORINI of the
Medhurst Apartments. Baumgarten, who has enjoyed no previous
newspaper experience, hopes to make money through the medium of
advertising matter which will appear in his publication, some
500 - 1000 copies of which will be printed when the thing is in
full swing. He is now residing at House 13, Lane 24, Ward Road.
The last four years have seen him in the role of a travelling
adventurer, unsuccessfully endeavouring to make a living in
Shanghai, Harbin, Mukden, Tientsin, Fusan, Manila, Java, Bangkok,
Hongkong and Kobe in hawking photographs and wood-cuts. As
recently as November 13, 1936, he was, according to the Shanghai
Nichi-nichi, expelled from Japan for the abduction of Japanese
females. Baumgarten arrived in Shanghai on November 14, 1936
on the "Nagasaki Maru" from Kobe where he admits that he was
detained by the police authorities for one night and then placed
by them on board the steamer in question. Baumgarten's version
of his expulsion from Japan - which is probably more correct

现随函附上一份“Deutsche Wochenschau”的样刊，这是一份新的
德文/英文四版报纸，计划于1936年12月初在当地首次发行。
其基调为非政治性，版面将致力于时事新闻和插图。
该刊物未得到任何当地官方德国机构的支持或资助，这些机构
认为，《东亚劳埃德报》（Ostasiatischer Lloyd）作为一份报纸，
已足以满足此地德国社区的需求。
“Deutsche Wochenschau”的编辑和出版人是一位德国人，
Martin BAUMGARTEN，36年前出生于布赖斯高地区弗赖堡。
他不是犹太人。参与这项新闻 ventures 作为隐名合伙人的是
麦赫斯特公寓（Medhurst Apartments）的 Dr. von MIORINI。
Baumgarten 此前没有任何报纸工作经验，希望通过在其出版物中
刊登广告来赚钱，当业务全面展开时，印刷量约为500至1000份。
他目前居住在华德路24弄13号。
在过去四年里，他一直扮演着一名流浪冒险家的角色，在上海、
哈尔滨、奉天、天津、釜山、马尼拉、爪哇、曼谷、
香港和神户兜售照片和木刻版画，但未能成功谋生。
据《上海日日新闻》报道，就在1936年11月13日，他因
绑架日本女性而被日本驱逐出境。Baumgarten 于1936年11月14日
乘“长崎丸”号从神户抵达上海，他承认在神户被警察当局
拘留了一晚，随后被他们送上该轮船。Baumgarten 对其被日本
驱逐的说法——这可能比

than that appearing in the Japanese daily - was that he was
compelled to leave by the police owing to the fact that he was
one month behind in the payment of his hotel bill and that he
was without means of subsistence.
Several complaints have been received by the German
Consular Authorities here from their colleagues in the Far
East vis-a-vis Baumgarten's mode of soliciting charity from
various benevolent organisations, and in general he is regarded
by them as an adventurer or "cheap crook."
His political convictions are such that will apparently
not cause the Police any trouble. He states that he is not
a follower of Nazism or a member of the party, but on the other
hand is not inclined towards communism, although to use his
own words......"...in German circles you must be one or the
other....there is no in-between...."
He is in possession of German Passport No. 9/34 issued
at Bangkok on March 13, 1934.
General observation will be maintained regarding his
movements and his newspaper, which, i. should be mentioned,
will be published weekly, and anything of interest from a
Police point of view, will form the subject of a further report.

日本日报上刊登的版本更为准确——是他因拖欠酒店账单一个月
且无生计来源，被迫由警察勒令离开。
此地德国领事当局收到了其在远东的同僚关于 Baumgarten
向各种慈善组织乞讨方式的几起投诉，总体而言，他们将他
视为一名冒险家或“低级骗子”。
他的政治信仰显然不会给警方带来任何麻烦。他声称自己
不是纳粹主义的追随者或党员，但另一方面也不倾向
于共产主义，尽管用他自己的话说......“...在德国圈子里，
你必须是其中之一....没有中间道路....”
他持有1934年3月13日在曼谷签发的德国护照，号码为 9/34。
将对他的行踪及其报纸保持一般性观察，顺便提一句，该报
将每周出版，任何从警方角度看有趣的事项，将成为进一步
报告的主题。
S.5.

Frauen und Kinder aus Madrid
abtransportiert
MADRID, November 22. — (Reuters). —Um unnötige
Gefahren für die Civilbevölkerung zu vermeiden und die Ver-
pflegung der Einwohner und Truppen zu erleichtern, hat das
Verteidigungskomitee Maurids die zwangsweise Räumung der
Stadt von der Civilbevölkerung angeordnet.
Erfolge der Loyalisten.
MADRID, November 22. — Havas berichtet, daß
die Loyalisten das Universitätsgebäude (Casa Velaquez) im
Norden Madrids zurückerobert haben. Die Einnahme hat
strategische Bedeutung, gleichwohl das Gebäude der Univer-
sität durch die Beschießung vollständig zerstört worden ist.

Vor der Beschießung Barcelonas
PERPIGNAN, November 22. — (Reuters). — Eine große
Zahl Reisender traf hier von Barcelona ein wegen der An-
kündigung General Francos, den Hafen zu beschießen. Man
fürchtet, die Bombardierung Barcelonas steht unmittelbar be-
vor. Der französische Konsul hat angesichts der drohenden
Gefahr alle französischen Staatsbürger angewiesen, die Stadt
zu verlassen.

All Non-Combatants To Be Sent From
Beleaguered Madrid
MADRID, Nov. 22.—(Reuters).—Both to avoid unneces-
sary risks to the civil population and to reduce the difficulties
of provisioning the inhabitants and troops, the Defense Com-
mittee today ordered the compulsory evacuation of all women,
children and non-combatants from Madrid.
Loyalists Recapture Area
MADRID, Nov. 22.—(Havas).—Loyalist forces have now
completely recaptured Casa Velazquez, French-owned building
in the University City on the northwestern outskirts of Madrid,
Havas special correspondent, M. Christian Ozanne reports.
The capture is of strategic importance, but the building
itself is now little more than a mass of ruins, as it burned
almost to the ground following intense bombardment reports.

Bombarding Of Barcelona Feared Near
Many Evacuation In Face Of Threat By Franco
PERPIGNAN, Nov. 22.—(Reuters).—Large numbers of
travellers have arrived here from Barcelona, having with-
drawn because of the threat made by General Francisco Franco,
the insurgent generalissimo, to bombard the port.
Some of the travellers expressed fears that the bombard-
ment was imminent.

妇女和儿童从马德里
撤离
马德里，11月22日。—（路透社）。—为避免平民遭受不必要
的危险，并 облегчить 居民和军队的补给，马德里
防御委员会下令强制疏散城市中的平民人口。
忠诚派的成功。
马德里，11月22日。—哈瓦斯社报道，
忠诚派已收复马德里北部的大学建筑（Casa Velaquez）。此次占领具有
战略意义，尽管大学建筑已在炮击中完全被毁。

巴塞罗那遭炮击前夕
佩皮尼昂，11月22日。—（路透社）。—由于佛朗哥将军宣布
要炮击港口，大量旅客从巴塞罗那抵达此处。人们
担心对巴塞罗那的轰炸迫在眉睫。鉴于迫在眉睫的
危险，法国领事已指示所有法国公民离开该市。

所有非战斗人员将被送出
被围困的马德里
马德里，11月22日。—（路透社）。—既为避免平民人口遭受不必要
的风险，也为减少向居民和军队提供补给的困难，防御委
员会今日下令强制疏散马德里所有妇女、儿童和非战斗人员。
忠诚派收复区域
马德里，11月22日。—（哈瓦斯社）。—据哈瓦斯社特约记者
M. Christian Ozanne 报道，忠诚派部队现已完全收复位于马德里
西北郊大学城内的法资建筑 Casa Velazquez。
此次占领具有战略意义，但该建筑本身现在几乎只剩下一片废墟，
据报道，在猛烈轰炸后，它几乎被夷为平地。

担心巴塞罗那即将遭炮击
面对佛朗哥的威胁，许多人撤离
佩皮尼昂，11月22日。—（路透社）。—大量旅客已从巴塞罗那抵达
此处，他们因叛军总司令弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥将军威胁要炮击
港口而撤离。
部分旅客表示担心轰炸迫在眉睫。
